results.label: this tree ships the M111 calendar-read state vocabulary (the committed parent does not, and that absence is this probe's control)
a calendar that WAS read and holds nothing that touches this symbol reads as `clear`, with no unavailability anywhere
an empty feed is reported by the market layer as a failure (its own "empty calendar" error), not as a quiet week with zero rows
so it reaches the news check as `unknown` too — counting rows cannot manufacture an all-clear
the outage is real at the source: the market layer refuses the read rather than serving an empty week
the outage reaches the news check as `unknown` — NOT as a quiet calendar
and the reason travels with it, so a caller never has to say "unknown" without saying why
the payload carries the module's own sentence rather than a second wording invented here
the failure is NOT dressed as data: no events, no upcoming list, and the currencies still name the symbol's own
the two windows are STILL echoed on the unknown path, so an outage can never be read as "the window was applied and nothing was found"
the windows also say the read failed, beside the pair they belong to
the old `error` key is still there AND still names the read, so a consumer written against the previous shape is not silently blinded
the payload still has no top-level single knob: M111 added states, it did not resurrect a number
a thrown read is the SAME outcome as `{ok:false}` — one unknown state, not two behaviours
the thrown message is the reason, quoted rather than replaced by a generic phrase
a thrown read does not escape the engine: no exception reaches a route, and the pair is still echoed
even a non-Error throw is stringified into a readable reason rather than leaking a bare value
a release INSIDE the block is still `blocked` with the M110 sentence, so the new state did not replace the old rule
the asymmetric boundaries are untouched by M111: the 45-minute print is blocked on the settle side, 46 is let go
an outage and a block are both READS: every table is byte-identical afterwards, and an unknown never becomes a stored fact
the engine states the three outcomes at the function it happens in, so the rule is readable where it is applied

scope: M111 engine: a read that failed is unknown, a read that worked is clear: actual runtime/auth/SQL/HTTP with a frozen UTC clock, a synthetic calendar fed through the app's own parser and a patched market module for the thrown-read path; M111 calendar-read states (blocked/clear/unknown), no provider/broker/pixel/human proof and no claim about what a release does to price
